text_fidelity_a:
Brain Games - The Game - Based on the Emmy Nominated National Geographic Channel TV Series This game is rated for 3-6 players ages 14+. However, my boyfriend and I were able to play by just leaving out the head-to-head (challenge cards) for each category.

The object of the game is to be the first one to win a game piece in all four game categories. I love board games and so does my boyfriend, which is why I got this. At the beginning we found playing this game nearly impossible. Neither one of us watch TV (this is based on a TV series) nor have cable. Therefore, it took us a while to even understand what this was about and what many of the game cards were asking us to do. We kept asking ourselves “Are we really that stupid?” However, after playing for almost 2 hours, we were enlightened. Nevertheless, for the uninitiated, this game might be challenging and confusing the first time around. After that not so much because then one remembers how to solve most of the cards and when that happens, this game will have to be “retired” for a while.

Below is a sentence on the box top which provides a good, yet very simple, idea of what “brain games” are all about.
THINK YOU
YOU CAN'T
BE FOOLED?
You just were. Read it again.

If you did not find the double YOU in the phrase on the first try, then you were fooled.

WHAT'S IN THE BOX:
- 192 game cards consisting of 48 cards each in each of the 4 categories (mind & body, language, logic, vision)
- A "box topper" with 4 game slots to hold the cards
- 40 hexagon shaped game tiles (8 tiles for each category, 4 wild, and 4 lose-a-turn)
- 6 pawns (playing pieces)
- 6 score cards
- 1 game board in 4 puzzle pieces
- 1 die that holds numbers 1, 2, & 3 only (two times)

Everything is made of cardboard except for the pawns and die. The score cards and puzzle pieces are easily punched out of the cardboard card provided.

In summary, this game is good for those who like to be challenged or know what the game is about. However, if you play this several times, you'll probably remember the answers and have to put this away for about one year before playing it again.
text_fidelity_b: Brain Games - The Game - Based on the Emmy Nominated National Geographic Channel TV Series

text_fidelity_a: CGE Czech Games Edition Codenames Boardgame This game is best played with 4 people (two teams of two).  Your partner tries to prompt you to pick the correct cards on the table between you by giving you a single word clue and telling you how many cards on the table it relates to.  You need to decipher the hint by figuring out which of the cards they means, but don't pick the wrong one!  It could end up giving a point to the other team or if you pick the one "black card" on the table it ends the game and you instantly lose.  This game is endlessly creative and challenging as the word cards on the table and which cards correspond to your team will always be different each game.  The creative part is figuring out new ways to bundle the most cards together with a single word so you can find all your teams cards before the other team finds theirs.  It's a race to figure out the code!

text_fidelity_a:
CALOVER Gift Toys for Kids Cat Dog Remote Control Mock Rat Mouse Mice Prank Gag Funny Practical Joke Toy for Holiday Party Late last year, for a week or so, all 3 of our cats sat gathered around the stove in the kitchen just staring at it. I quickly figured that was probably NOT a good sign-that we likely had an uninvited guest in our home. A few days later, I was proven correct. Got up early one morning to take the dog out and there was a dead mouse by the front door waiting to greet me, with 2 of the 3 cats sitting close by, proud of what they had left for me. (I don't think I've ever screamed louder in my entire life than I did that morning! lolol-I did heap praise on them after I calmed down) Unfortunately, the cats were once again gathered around the stove watching...and a few days later, mouse #2 was waiting for us to clean up. (Thank God I didn't find that one)

As soon as I saw this cat toy, I immediately ordered it. Though one of our 3 cats who helped catch the mice has since gone to the Rainbow Bridge, I knew the other 2, Miss Piggy and Squeaky, would have loads of fun playing with this toy. (And if I'm being honest, I want to keep them in tip-top shape in case any further 'uninvited guests' find their way into our home! lol) The mouse (I see it more of a rat than a mouse) is nearly 11 inches long from the tip of the nose to the end of the tail. It has beady red eyes that light up. From a distance, I believe people (who don't know its fake) could mistaken it for a real mouse (rat). It has gray fur and what appears to be sharp teeth sticking out of its mouth. (The teeth are NOT sharp, they only appear that way) The mouse takes 3 AAA batteries (not included) and the remote controller takes 2 AAA batteries as well. (not included) The only assembly required is placing the batteries in the mouse and controller. A nice, small screwdriver comes with the toy, something I especially appreciate! (Works on my eyeglass hinges as well!) The controller allows you to move the mouse forward and backward. (Both of our young kids were able to operate the remote control without issue while we stood with them) It does work on carpet but works far better on flooring. As soon as we turned it on and began steering it around the room, 2 cats immediately popped out of their beds, their curiosity piqued. Both cats watched the mouse zip around the floor for a bit. As soon as it got close to Miss Piggy, she jumped and ran under the bed. lol. But Squeaky...he was far braver than Piggy and watched it up close. We'd stop it for awhile and he'd creep closer and closer to it, staring at it....and then we'd start it up again. lol. It was loads of fun to watch him with this toy. It certainly kept him entertained for quite some time! Piggy stayed hidden but she's a nosy cat...she'll get the hang of it before long.

This is a fun toy not only for cats but for cat owners to operate for their cats! We had loads of fun watching the cat's reaction. Its a great way for your cat to get some exercise as well. Very easy to operate also!

UPDATE******************

We got this out again tonight to play with. This time, the dog had more fun chasing it than the cats. However, after just under 15 minutes of use, it stopped working entirely! Even though I had used brand new batteries in the mouse and the controller when I first got it (a day ago), I replaced all 5 batteries. It does NOT work at all. Nothing happened to it. It did not fall, it didn't' crash, it was not damaged in any way, it simply stopped working altogether in the blink of an eye. And that's a darn shame because my cat AND dog had fun with it. Due to the fact that it stopped working entirely after just under 30 minutes of total use since we got it, and the fact we did nothing to break it/make it stop working, I've changed my rating/review of this item. I cannot recommend an item that stops working out of the blue as this did. For the minutes that it did work, my pets loved it. And we loved watching them have fun.
text_fidelity_b: CALOVER Gift Toys for Kids Cat Dog Remote Control Mock Rat Mouse Mice Prank Gag Funny Practical Joke Toy for Holiday Party

Hot Wheels Track Set with 1:64 Scale Toy Firetruck, City Fire Station with Dragon Nemesis and Track Play, Dragon Drive Firefight We've owned plenty of hotwheels sets, some pretty standard and some pretty creative. This is one of those interesting ones I couldn't really understand until we got it. The car is sort of on an "assisted loop", in that there are points that require your intervention to continue. It starts off being "spit out" by the dragon, then fired from a booth, then launched up a loop, and- if everything goes according to plan - it lands on the head of the dragon which will either fall forward or to the side (not knowing which way is part of the fun). However, if you don't have everything 100% seated properly, it just fails miserably. My kids had trouble getting it to work until I came and reseated some parts more forcefully, but even then we still had a few misfires that caused it not to work.
But I suppose that's the tradeoff of the more obscure track sets, sometimes they are more difficult to operate successfully. Part of the fun is making it work, I think. But if you have a kid who isn't up for that challenge, maybe this isn't the set for them. We actually really liked it, and the payoff when it DOES work is the sort of moment that gets high fives and cheers all around.

text_fidelity_a:
Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game Onitama is a 2-player only game that tries to have a theme, but is really quite abstract.

When I heard about it, I was really quite intrigued that this would be added to the Dice Tower Essentials line as an abstract; after all, isn't Tom Vasel the guy who dislikes most abstracts because they're not theme-y enough? Yet here is the third game in his very quality game series that is otherwise highly thematic, and he goes with an abstract. Seemed like the game must be incredible to have cracked that list as an abstract.

I played a number of times with my wife, who admittedly likes this game quite a lot more than I do. I find the game similar to chess or the Duke, in which you have a certain number of moves, represented by cards, and you move your pieces around the board, switching cards with your opponent along the way. There is a lot of doublethink - If I do this, then they know I'll do that next turn, so they might do this... - and I like that element of the game, but the limitation on my moves did tend to cramp my style a little more, and I'd find myself wishing I just had more options. That skill can probably be built up over time playing with this one, but I don't know if it grabbed me enough to make me invest my time with it.

If 3.5 were an option, I'd go with that. Just not my style, and not as good as the expectations led me to believe.
text_fidelity_b: Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game

Everything you need to create a pirate themed creature is included on each page.
There are 4 designs and 6 sheets of each design.
The pirate, octopus, or parrot sticker set can be done on the back of the sticker sheet or on a completely separate sheet of paper.
I really like that the stickers are not super hard to get off of the sheet.
The stickers can be moved after they are initially stuck to the page - this is helpful as my kids like to change their mind!
This is a great activity for my 3yo or 5yo to do when I need them to have some quiet time.
These would also be great as a part of a care package.
I will be using these as part of a Valentine’s Day gift for my kids’ classmates - instead of handing out candy to their classmates.
I like that each page has multiple options so even though there are 6 of the same sticker sheets, each of them can be completely different.
If I had to change anything about this set it would be that the sticker sheets didn’t include anything alcohol related.
Since I want to send these to school I can’t use the parrot sheets as they have a RUM bottle on them.
The pirate with the boat has a bottle as well but the bottle has a skull and cross bones so it could be anything pirate related.

ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay Wow! there are a few things I love in games; easy to learn rules, ability to ages, and uniqueness. This comes up in spades for all of those and you can add a healthy dose of collaboration. It is so much better to see kids working together than squabbling. We played this game through twice and the kids were super engaged. Ages 9=17 and a middle aged parent and we all enjoyed it. It is wonderfully unique along the lines of ICE COOL which we got about this time last year.

The games is super well constructed. I love the lantern, the sturdy trees, and the awesome little woodland animals. I also love the it is play completely in the dark. This is a perfect game for the tent or dark winters evening. It is wonderfully moody.

I don't know that this is a game that will be brought out a lot, but I highly recommend it. This game rocks in its simple uniqueness.

I recently met someone who weaves huge items and after seeing photos of her work my interest in weaving was renewed. I like the simplicity of these looms but do have some comments. Firstly, the frame is wood with plastic pegs. A screw in each corner holds the frame together but mine is a bit loose. I may need to tighten later. Instruction booklet is well written, read all the way through before starting because there are tips later on in the booklet. Parents please note that every other row you must insert a second flat shed stick into the loom. It's not complicated, just takes time so be aware if your child may not have patience to do this.
My only complaint is I ordered the bigger size B loom and in the photo on Amazon it showed yarn in orange, yellow and reds so I bought a refill yarn kit called Sierra because it was black and red and I thought it would be nice to have both but when my loom arrived I see the size B comes with the black and red yarn and the smaller sized A has the oranges. So now I'll have two black and red items :( I don't know where the photo came from but it should be corrected!
The manufacturers website shows the correct colors but I didn't go there until after I got my loom. I would also recommend spending $10 more to get the Wonderloom. It helps push the yarn down evenly.
This loom is a good size for making place mats.

PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based) I gave this PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Building and Coding - Construction Kit with Puzzles, Augmented Reality to my 7 year old son as a gift from Santa. In comparison to other robot building kits, I wasn't that impressed. First of all, you MUST have an updated iOs or Android phone/tablet. I am unsure if Android has this problem, but if you have an iPhone 5 or 6 and you can't update to the latest iOs, you will not be able to use this robot. Also, since this is an augmented reality app, I doubt that the Kindle Fire will work on this. The camera just isn't powerful enough. I ran into this problem with my son's Fire HD 10 for other AR programs. Next, when you unbox, there are no instructions. You have to go a website to get the instruction manual, which could have been printed on the two cards in the box that say go to the website for a manual. Finally, this does not come with a power source. There is a lithium battery and a USB cable, but you will have to have your own plug. Obviously, many of us will already have various plugs, but to have a designated plug would be nice considering the amount asked for this product.

Overall, my son's interest in this was limited. He's much more interested using his other building toys and finding ways for them to move. I think he feels limited in his creativity. You cannot use this without the App, so any ideas he has of incorporating other mediums to this has him frustrated. It's a nice idea. However, considering that I try to limit his screen time as well it would be nice to have an off screen option to play with this.
text_fidelity_b: PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based)

Melissa & Doug Princess Design Activity Kit - 9 Double-Sided Plates, 4 Colored Pencils, Rubbing Crayon When I was a kid, I had one of these fashion plate toys. It was fun. You set the outfit, rub the crayon over it, then color it. So, although the primary purpose of this toy is vanity, I like the creative and artistic aspect of it. My 6 year old daughter was thrilled when she saw it. The packaging leaves much to be desired. It is a clamshell package. I took it out, showed her how it worked, and set her to work on creating some outfits. There are 3 bottom plates (6 options), 3 top plates (6 options), and 3 head plates (6 options). All the plates fit inside a little drawer. It comes with one crayon to rub with an attachment so you don't have to get your fingers all messy and 4 colored pencils.

This is super cheap quality. The lid only closes (on the top) when you have the drawer pushed in. The plates themselves are not exactly even, they are a bit warped and don't lay flat. The drawing area is too small for a regular sheet of paper, but slightly larger than half a sheet of paper. You cut paper in half to use half sheets and they slide around a bit in the top area. Since the plates are a bit warped, you can't get a good rubbing of the pictures. (One skirt and top is polka dotted and not even half the dots will transfer to the paper.) The top is difficult to open. It also easily pops off on the opposite side that should not be opening. The eyes usually don't transfer to the rubbing either.

The colored pencils it comes with are pretty poor quality and not good color choices. (Brown, indigo, light pink, and yellow.) They don't have very much pigment in them and you're coloring on top of a rubbing, so you need much more vivid pencils than it comes with.

Within about 20 minutes of use, my 6 year old had already found the duct tape and taped the lid down. She likes the product and said other girls would like it too, just use duct tape.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Princess Design Activity Kit - 9 Double-Sided Plates, 4 Colored Pencils, Rubbing Crayon

VTech PJ Masks Super Learning Headquarters My 4-year-old LOVES this toy. He calls it his "PJ Masks Computer" and wants to play with it constantly. Even when he's not allowed to turn it on (before we leave in the morning), he plays with the vehicles and has a great time. He loves packing it with him in the car, and the sides act as convenient handles for carrying. Do note that the vehicles are not locked down in any way, and are prone to falling off and getting lost if carried around or dumped on the ground in a car tantrum.

Unpackaging the toy is fairly straightforward: you'll need scissors and a screwdriver (or coin). Once you remove it from the box and cardboard packing, you'll find two screws on the back that lock in the Gekko-Mobile and Owl Glider. These unscrew easily with a screwdriver or coin. Catboys vehicle is secured with a zip tie that requires cutting. The toy comes with demonstration batteries (2 AA). They recommend you replace them for full play

The toy is easy to play with. Select your car (character), choose a mode (Vehicle, Science, and Problem Solving) and select a location (Park, Fun Fair, Museum, and Headquarters). There are three activities and four locations, resulting in a total of 12 activities. The games vary and involve avoiding obstacles, sorting items, matching, completing patterns, and learning facts.

This toy is recommended for ages 3-6. Some of the games feel advanced for the younger age range but will give them something to grow into while keeping the 6-year-olds engaged. I'm not sure that my 4 yo really "gets" some of the games, but that doesn't stop him. My 7 yo really loves to play this when she gets a chance.

Like any interactive toy, the volume is higher than necessary. You can adjust the volume (press the volume button, click the car to the left a few times, then click the windshield to set the volume level). Even at the lowest setting, it still feels too loud. It's not too bad if you are a few feet away, or it's in the back seat of the car.
text_fidelity_b: VTech PJ Masks Super Learning Headquarters

Hot Wheels Track Builder Unlimited Slide & Launch Pack for Kids 6 Years & Older with a 1:64 Scale Hot Wheels Vehicle, Moveable Kicker Booster & 3 Track Pieces that Connect to Other Sets This is a redesign of previous Track Builder Loop Kicker, and it does same job - a rubber band powered leg gets triggered by car passing through to "kick" the car faster through the loop - but this one changes the pieces. Gone is the ball-joint of the center tower track mount from the older version (mount is still there, but fixed to flat position), and the 2 track pieces and center connector that make up the loop have been replaced by 2 fixed, hinged pieces of pre-curved plastic that snap together. Redesign comes with 2 less pieces of flat track.

Pros
- Kicker loop quicker to assemble than previous version
- Loop doesn't flex as much as old version, so cars keep more speed through the loop
- Includes 2 pieces of straight, low-sidewall track
- Includes 4 newest track connector pieces despite not needing any
- Includes 1 car that works with track (not all Hot Wheels work with all track sets)
- Kicker leg has a safety hinge so a second car can pass under it

Neutral
- The included car is an easily-found 2019 basic release, the mint Speed Blur series version of Exotique

Cons
- Isn't that much faster than just setting up or taking down track
- When folded down, takes up more space than the older one where you disassembled track
- Not that easy to remove the center tower from the base
- Smaller base is harder to put weights on to keep the track from moving when it kicks
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Unlimited Slide & Launch Pack for Kids 6 Years & Older with a 1:64 Scale Hot Wheels Vehicle, Moveable Kicker Booster & 3 Track Pieces that Connect to Other Sets

text_fidelity_a:
YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls [[VIDEOID:258489d4261f7a5b0f26535ccf27c4f9]] The plusses: The game is beautiful to look at and feels good quality. The print quality is very very good, these cards do not feel cheap, they feel almost like fancy plastic. It’s also a standard size which means if you are heavy users it’s not challenging to find sleeves to accommodate. I’m also pretty sure the box is big enough to handle sleeves. The rules are relatively simple, and the instruction manual provides a QR code that leads to a video of the gameplay combined with errata to the rules as written. You will *need* the errata because the rules do not answer very basic questions. It makes me wonder how much this was play-tested with strangers before release. It’s great to see a company offering solid support after release though!

At more than 100 cards, the deck is very unwieldy to shuffle, this is definitely one that needs to be broken into smaller piles to handle and then combined.

The rounds are much shorter than expected, some rounds were over in a 2 player game in as little as three fast turns. The actual gameplay is not one “game” but to have the least points over the series of many rounds (the most “loses” the game night.) There was very little tension or any emotional investment because of the fast turnover–that might work for some folks but it didn’t feel like it was worth working on big words without stalling. There were two rounds where the game was over in two turns before my husband could even play a card. It feels like more luck than skill which is not desirable in a word game. My biggest criticism is that due to the number of repeated vowels, gameplay can feel repetitive, we started round after round with “e” or “a” despite shuffling many times. I would love to see a second deck of a different color with starting letters distributed in a more logical way because the starting letter affects the gameplay variety over time. My husband and I love wordplay and puns as a rule and this game was not skill-based enough for the two-player version for us to want to invest too much more time on it. Maybe if we played it for longer there would be more to it but we both got bored after playing 10 or so rounds and probably wouldn’t give it a second try.

The idea itself is an awesome one, when it works it’s like combining scrabble with Uno. There is solid product quality and marketing. It just lacked the skill vs luck factor for us, which may be personal taste

I really think this game needs some tweaks to the gameplay to make it better before I’d really recommend it, at least on the game shelf of a couple. It says ages 8 and up, but I can’t imagine playing this with my almost 8yo, especially without eliminating some of the rules regarding “made up words” because 50 points penalty is pretty punitive for what might be an accidental misspelling, and even with some coaching it would be pretty difficult (And my kiddo has an above-average vocabulary). Maybe several 8yo together do well? We may try to break it out at a party among adults in the future.
text_fidelity_b: YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls

text_fidelity_a: Foxnovo Universal Tall Landing Gear Skid for DJI F450 F550 Sk480 Multirotor Quadcopter These legs are the perfect upgrade for the Syma X8C (white) if you're going to be using a different camera. The stock legs are just too short to allow you to mount any kind of adjustable camera rigging and GoPro type camera. You will need to do some drilling in these legs (and shave off the mounting alignment flange of the quad) to make them fit. But, it's worth it. This pic is of the same legs (black) on my Syma X8G (same body as the C, just a different color) and these legs on my Syma X8C. These legs give you the spread and stability you need, as well as the height. They're rigid, strong and don't weigh much more than the stock legs. I've seen some negative reviews regarding 'flimsiness'. I think that anyone should keep in mind the original configuration calls for bracing between the legs, in such a way that actually provides more structural integrity to each leg. Therefore, no bracing means less rigidity, the greater the chances of breakage. Having said that, I've been flying my Syma X8 quads with these for a while now. One of which was totaled. Seriously, the quad dropped like a rock from about 150 feet, crashing through trees and broke HARD. I had to do a total rebuild with new body, motor mounts, gears, etc.The only parts re-used were the control board and motors and the LEGS, which DID NOT BREAK!
text_fidelity_b: Foxnovo Universal Tall Landing Gear Skid for DJI F450 F550 Sk480 Multirotor Quadcopter

QTL School Stickers for Teacher Stickers for Students Laptop Kids Water Bottles Stickers Science Stickers Waterproof Back to School Stickers Packs 50Pcs I love sending Halloween cards but they don't seem complete without great stickers.

I have tried MANY kinds over the years, and THESE, are BY FAR, the BEST.

PROS:

SIZE - BIG I got exclusively for putting on envelopes, and most of them where so big, I could only put on back to seal. You may consider that a plus or minus, but they STICK out!

ADHESIVE - I noticed someone put they just have PAPER on the back and they had to glue them down. I have a feeling they just didn't realize you have to pull the paper off. The adhesion is GREAT.

PACKAGING AND PRESENTATION - Most stickers are on a sheet or a roll, these all came separately in a little packet. SO easy. I wish more stickers came this way.

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Toy Car Track Set Hill Climb Champion with 1:64 Scale Car, Launch Uphill to Score Points & Win Amazon was temporarily out of stock so I grabbed this from another source. We are an avid Hot Wheels family and always like to check out the newer sets. I love the idea of running a car around a course continuously, without relying on batteries. This set comes with a big launcher, that features a unique track with protruding tabs that catch the cars from behind as you blast them around the track. The whole idea is to catch the car(s) at the right time when it reenters the launcher, so you can have it racing around the course non-stop. Unfortunately, the course is too small and uninteresting, yet, if the layout was much larger, that launcher wouldn't have enough force without some kind of midway helper (like an automatic loop launcher). This would make a world of a difference in fun, so you you're not pounding the launcher every half second to keep the car circulating around a tiny oval which gets old fast.

Big annoyance: The launcher is very tall, so it comes in packed in two pieces which easily lock together, however, once locked, you're unable to seperate them. This is now the second set we have with this annoying problem. We like storing our hot wheels in their boxes, but once opened, there's no way to get this giant launcher back inside. Even if storing out of the box, with other toys, it's a big jalopy that could have been dismantled, taking up less space.

And finally, kids need laser-sharp hand/eye coordination to catch the car on time, so this may frustrate the impatient type. When you do manage to catch the car to keep it going, it does feel rewarding, even if it's only 2 laps. We haven't tried more than one car at a time, but I imagine on a large course, it must be fun, but on this small circuit, it's probably near impossible to work with.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Toy Car Track Set Hill Climb Champion with 1:64 Scale Car, Launch Uphill to Score Points & Win

They are quite unique. At 339 pieces, this one is rather large. One might thing that it might not take that long to put together. . .but. . . they would be incorrect. Each piece is different. . . Different size. . . Different shape. . . and so on. Some of the pieces are quite small, so not good around small children. Though this puzzle does make for a nice family activity. You’ll notice that some of these pieces are actually animal shape.

Though there are lots of these puzzles being sold by Chinese companies on Amazon. . . .There’s one thing that differentiates them . . . and that’s the packaging. This one has a very nice pressed-wood box. You can choose to use the box for the puzzle. . . or. .. for other things. Some Chinese sellers offer just a simple cardboard box, so this is certainly the preferred packaging.

This puzzle is Made in China. At the current price of 70 bucks. . . It’s well over twice the price it should be. Nice, but certainly very overpriced.

Creative Kids Air Dry Clay Modeling Crafts Kit for Children - Super Light Nontoxic - 30 Vibrant Colors & 3 Clay Tools - STEM Educational DIY Molding Set – Gift for Boys & Girls 4+ We go through a lot of air dry clay in our house since we are homeschooling, and the kids really love making gifts for one another, toy food for their dolls, decorations for holidays, etc. It's been a really fun way of learning how to make items destined to be dried and kept, rather than just mushing colors together and playing like you do with play dough.

This set has a huge array of colors laid out in a rainbow, and it is very inspiring and gorgeous to look at. It would make a very delightful gift. I really appreciate that it comes with keychain findings as well as a few tools to use when crafting.

The huge quantity of colors is the big selling point of this kit, and the quality of the clay was great, soft and just the right texture. The one downside is that it is a little tough to get it out of the packaging without it all sticking together and my children needed assistance with this, and it doesn't come with little plastic containers, rather you have to shove each color into a little Ziploc bag after use, which I think makes it dry out faster than the sets that come with the plastic tub to store each color in.

I would recommend this as a set to get for the family after you've purchased a set that comes with the little tubs. Then, as your children are wanting a new color because they've used another color up, they can choose from the enormous array of rainbow hues available in this set. Because this set has seriously the most inspiring rainbow layout of colors I've seen.

text_fidelity_a:
The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe) The resistance is a fantastic game with a great price and superb components. The rules are very simple also so the game can be picked up by nearly anyone in a matter of minutes. A sample round will remove any doubt about the rules and is often the best way I have found to teach the game.

So what is this about? The Resistance is a game of guessing and deduction that is rules light and fun heavy. In the basic game 5 to 10 players take on the role of either good guys or bad guys by being dealt cards that depict their character. Good guys or the resistance are blue and spies are red. The ratio of spies to resistance is driven by the number of players in a game. The spies always have fewer allies in the game than do the resistance players.

Once the players have secretly looked at their role card, everyone closes their eyes. The first player commands everyone to close their eyes, he then commands the spies and only the spies to open their eyes and look around to identify each other, he then commands them to close their eyes and lastly commands everyone to open their eyes.

So now the spies know who each other are but the allies have no idea.

The game is then played as 5 simple 'missions'. A mission consists of the first player choosing a number
of players to 'go on the mission'. The number is dependent on how many total players are playing. The more players, the more involved in each mission. Each mission from 1 to 5 will have gradually more players involved.

Everyone votes to allow or disallow the chosen players to go on the mission. Each player will have two cards to vote
with each round. These cards are marked clearly with symbols to indicate if you do or do not agree to allow the chosen players to play.

Here is where the game gets going. If the vote fails to allow the chosen players to go on the mission twice in a row, the spies win automatically.

If the players allow the mission to go forward, those players involved get to either make the mission successful or to sabotage the mission. This is done my dealing each player involved in the mission two cards. One of each success and sabotage. They secretly place their cards into two piles. The mission result and the dead pile.

Spies can sabotage or succeed a mission and the resistance players MUST succeed the mission.

The majority of succeed of sabotage rules the mission.

Rounds continue like this until the spies or the resistance have a best 3 out of 5 missions won by their side.

Up until this point your first game might seem kinda boring. But just wait, almost immediately you will figure
out who your junior sleuths are! Finger pointing and accusations will begin to fly out of the most timid players
mouths!

You will find players who are just 100% certain they know who is who and are almost always wrong! You will find out that some of your friends are REALLY GREAT LIARS and some are REALLY POOR LIARS!

The compound the fun there is also a plot deck. The plot deck is simply a deck of cards that each round, one is dealt by the first player and he can give it to someone else or keep it.
These cards are things like 'look at someone else role card' or 'veto a vote'.

I initially thought the plot deck would be horrible but I was very wrong. The first time we pulled a card that let one player look at another players role card the player looked and claimed the other player was a spy. The player accused immediately did a double take and denied the allegation fervently!

We were back at square one but now had two more people we couldn't trust! FUN! FUN! FUN!

You cannot go wrong with this game unless you live in a convent full of people with ZERO personality who have had all their fun genes removed.

So if you are looking for an excellent game, with super components, short playing time, and an immeasurable amount of fun, look no further than this gem!
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe)

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice These dice are beautifully made of solid pine. Playing games with these are fun but play responsibly. Displaying the dice as works of art is equally as great.

Provided in the package:
- Six die that weigh a combined 4.6 pounds. (See the attached pictures for an idea of size relative to two of my cats and their water fountain.)
- A strong canvas pouch for carrying the dice.
- A folded one-page pamphlet with two game variations and a sample score card for copying.

Each die is beautiful and each "number point" (i.e. dots) on the same die face is painted a rich coffee brown or dark tan. However, the "number points" are various shades of coffee brown on each side of the same die, so there is a slight inconsistency in color there. Nevertheless, this does not take away from their beauty. One should discount the "life-sized" claim. They are large but all of them stacked three high, side-by-side, do not even reach the height of a poised cat as you can see from my photos. When used for play instead of art, the round edge of each die provides for a smooth roll and reduction of injury to property or person. Although this is rated for ages 6 and above, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND children, adults, and pets stay far back when rolling the dice.

My boyfriend and I played the first game on my inside carpet since it was raining outside. I made sure to remove any items that could break around the area we were playing and I had to keep shooing the cats away. I originally thought we had to roll all six die at once (which is impossible). Therefore, when playing the two games in the instructions, roll each die one at a time because they are too large to roll together. The instructions should say that, however, because the first thought I had is "How am I going to roll these six die all at once," when the instructions said "roll the dice"?

My boyfriend loved the dice and the game even though I won. Since each die is heavy, it is extremely important to throw each die gently. I can see unsupervised children or drunk adults throwing these at each other and causing serious damage or death. As long as everyone plays responsibly, hours of fun and friendly competition are awaiting those who play this lawn or carpeted basement "game."
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice
